behaviour: The merge check holds a merge on undeclared paths, stale links, broken logs or a confirmed example's failing test.
The merge check lists touched requirements lacking a fidelity judgment, advisory only, never changing the exit code.
A pre-push hook runs the merge check, leaving foreign hooks untouched.
The merge check is one lightweight process with no transactions or locks and a one-screen report.
Every host adapter serves one host-neutral turn API, with a CLI-only fallback.
Hosts install codex writes a thin idempotent Codex adapter that preserves foreign entries.
Hosts install pi renders a thin Pi extension mapping Pi events to plumb hook calls.
Hosts install hermes renders a thin Hermes plugin registering the plumb command and hooks.
A read-only MCP server over stdio exposes brief, relevant, show, explain, impact and drift.
The pi-agent-factory importer maps relations, features and NCs to links with symbol and test-node ends.
An imported record is confirmed only where an upstream human consent pins its current content.
The import is idempotent and previews a dry-run plan of changes.
The status line and first summary line render a one-line status card with a plain-language intent.
The full intent card shows only when it matters, with full, compact or off verbosity.
Every hook output passes one emitter that deduplicates lines and enforces a token budget.
Owner commands accept plain words, resolve them to records and answer in the owner's terms.
Confirm prepares full cards for records awaiting confirmation and never reads words itself.
The view command writes a generated Obsidian vault and canvas that never approves anything.
The align command judges each edge of a scope weakest first without changing any edge.
Every advertised owner verb is routed and its help exits zero; why aliases explain.
Confirmations resting on a message the agent recorded itself are labelled self-recorded wherever shown.
note: Overlaps SR-168 and SR-112 on owner-only words.

behaviour: New record IDs are reserved through a shared git ref so worktrees never collide.
Merge-fix renumbers colliding incoming IDs and rewrites the references the incoming side introduced.
The merge check reports ID collisions with the plain fix.
Every log entry is its own never-edited file under the log directory, hash-chained.
Migrating the old log files into per-entry files keeps every digest and reference unchanged.
A git merge driver merges record files field by field against the merge base.
A same-field content conflict becomes an intent conflict inside the record for the owner to resolve.
note: Dump lists SR-150 in its supersedes.

behaviour: A quick merge check holds open intent conflicts as cards for the owner's choice.
The owner is warned when another worktree or branch changes the same record.
Awareness reads other worktrees read-only, cheaply, through per-worktree cached files.
Intent in flight is shared as claims in a shared git ref.
Intent conflicts with other branches' claims are caught at capture, before implementation.
Plumb installs as a Claude Code plugin running its own private copy of its tools.
Init adopts a project; projects not adopted stay silent.
Projects set up the old way keep working and the plugin stays silent there until moved.
note: Transitional but still a stated behaviour.

behaviour: Plumb draws a status band, panel and cards inside Claude Code at the owner's level.
Confirm buttons record the owner's confirmation of exactly what was shown, proved by a session secret.
note: SR-112 restates button as an owner-only path.

behaviour: Plumb gives Claude its background once per session and shows nothing twice.
Every owner-needed capability has an owner entry point; internal mechanisms stay internal.
Owner-visible text names no shell command and speaks at the owner's level.
An unrelated request in the same message never blocks an ok.
note: SR-101 supersedes it with a reader model.

behaviour: A bare yes or option letter records what question or proposal it answered.
note: Overlaps SR-097 and SR-156 on short answers.

behaviour: The clarify read-back questions itself and labels assumptions rather than asking.
An intent can state when it is done, and plumb tells the agent what a request leaves open.
A big plan is structurally checked and repaired before it is offered for confirmation.
A requirement left with two versions after a merge is shown once, as a choice card.
A rejected read-back is recaptured, judged and offered again; it counts as no only when read so.
